//: Tina's colour calls. lib/colour.ts reads this BEFORE its own vocabulary. A NON-NULL entry always wins and ends the matching there. A NULL entry does something narrower, and the difference is the whole file: it means 'this SUFFIX is not a colour', which is a real recorded decision and not a gap - it stops the term coming back on the next review - but it does NOT mean 'this product has no colour'. The suffix is suppressed and the rest of the title is still read, so 'Luxury Black Cascade ... - LIMITED EDITION' is still black. Written by the review page that 'npm run colour:review' generates; safe to hand-edit. Same role as data/colour-leads.json and data/default-cut-brands.json. ONE LIMIT worth knowing before you type a term: a colourway suffix is only read when it is 2 to 25 characters long and is not size-shaped (lib/colorVariants.ts:74-81), so a longer term, or something like 'XL', is a silent no-op here - it can never match anything.
//terms: Keyed by the EXACT lowercased colourway suffix - the text after the ' - ' or inside the '(...)' at the end of a title, as lib/colorVariants.ts splits it. One entry fixes every row any brand ever names that way, including rows the nightly refresh has not added yet. The value is a colour family from lib/colour.ts (black grey white cream beige brown navy blue green yellow orange red pink purple multi), which is final and ends the matching, or null for 'not a colour', which only takes that suffix out of play - lib/colour.ts then reads the REST of the title exactly as it would for a suffix it did not recognise, and reports any hit there as a weak match.
//weakWords: Keyed by a SINGLE lowercased word, and applies only to a match found in the BODY of a title, never in the suffix. It exists so a word like 'rose' can be switched off where it is usually a style name ('Mystic Rose Hijab') while still working as a colourway ('... - Dusty Rose'). null switches the word off in the body; a family name forces that family instead. A null costs only that word: 'Rose Pink ...' is still pink, because lib/colour.ts steps over the switched-off 'Rose' and keeps reading the same colour's words in the rest of the title.
